children: Thailand’s current account recorded a deficit of USD 1.6 billion in July 2026, shifting from a surplus of USD 1.1 billion in the corresponding month a year earlier.

The trade balance swung to a deficit of USD 0.1 billion from a surplus of USD 2.7 billion in July 2025, as imports rose to USD 34.4 billion from USD 25.4 billion, outpacing the increase in exports to USD 34.3 billion from USD 28.1 billion.
Meanwhile, the deficit in net services, primary income, and secondary income held steady at USD 1.5 billion.

On the financial account, the overall balance shifted to a deficit of USD 3.6 billion from a surplus of USD 3.5 billion, despite an increase in the general government surplus to USD 0.9 billion and that of other depository corporations to USD 6.7 billion from USD 3.5 billion.

title: Thailand Current Account Swings to Deficit
